label: Paper theatre
description: Cut-paper figures with jointed limbs perform on layered paper backdrops, side-on like a toy theatre. Scenes change like painted flats sliding in, and names and dates appear on paper labels.
suits: history, biography, myths and legends, scripture stories
guide: STAGING: this film is a paper theatre, and it stages the story being told: its people, its places and its events, played out as a play. Where the narration turns to what it means today, stay in the theatre (the same figures in a new tableau, a single figure alone on the stage, a symbolic prop raised on a rod) rather than cutting to modern scenes. Every shot is staged side-on, like a toy theatre or a shadow play: flat, layered planes one behind another (backdrop, midground flats, figures, foreground pieces), figures mostly in profile or three-quarter, moving across the stage, not towards the camera. Figures are cut-paper puppets with jointed limbs held by split pins: they gesture, bow, point, walk and turn with the stiff, charming movement of puppets. Scene changes are theatrical: a new painted flat slides in, a paper curtain drops, the sun or moon is raised on a rod. The camera stays in front of the stage: slow pans along it and gentle push-ins, never going behind. Give a shot a caption when the narration introduces a person, a place or a year the viewer should hold on to ("Moses", "Kadesh, c. 1400 BC", "Deuteronomy 1:26"): only what the narration says, a few words. Leave it empty otherwise; most shots have none.
